summary: The native sketch solver can now report, for each parameter, whether the lasting equations determine it or leave it free to move, and constraint inspection uses that to say which sketch points and entities are fully defined. A probe rotates each parameter's unit row into the diagnosis factor and always restores it, but only proposes an answer. Each answer is certified against the group's own rows in compensated arithmetic whose rounding is bounded too, because the factor leaves out entries within the dependence distance and rounds. Determined means the certified projection of the parameter's unit vector onto the directions the equations leave free is at most the solver's dependence distance, 1e-10, so fixing the parameter would add only a dependent equation. Free means a direction certified to move every equation by at most that distance per unit moves the parameter by more than the certainty margin, 1e-7, allowing for how far the nearest exact free direction can differ from it. A parameter between the two, one without a certificate, and one left once the probes' own work allowance of 20,000,000 entries runs out are not analysed. Fixed parameters are determined, parameters no equation reads are free, and a group of full rank is all determined. Only groups that converged with their rank certain and no constraint of theirs conflicting are analysed, and nothing is analysed when the diagnosis is unavailable. The buffer protocol moves from version 5 to 6: an options word asks for the analysis and rejects unknown bits, and every reply ends with one definition code per parameter. In TypeScript, a point is defined when both coordinates are determined and under-defined when either is free. A line needs both endpoints, a circle its center and radius, and an arc its center and both endpoints. Only constraint inspection asks. Commits, previews and drags do not ask, a drag cannot, and their answers are unchanged bit for bit. cad_inspect_sketch_constraints point and entity rows gain definition: defined, under-defined or unknown, and its analysis summary gains definition counts. There is no UI change.
warning: Potentially breaking for agents that validate cad_inspect_sketch_constraints replies strictly: point rows, entity rows and the points nested in relation and entity rows gain a definition field, and the analysis summary gains a definition object with defined, underDefined and unknown counts for points and entities. Every existing field keeps its name, shape and meaning. An agent that rejects unknown fields must accept them. The native sketch solver buffer protocol moves from version 5 to 6. The app and its bundled module change together, and as before a module that speaks another protocol is refused with a reload message, never used. The sketch worker's solved reply can carry diagnostics.definition, only for input that asks; the worker and the app ship together and both validate it strictly. No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD schema, storage or journal change. The native buffer protocol is version 6: the input header gains an options word after the equation count, whose only bit asks for definition, and the reply gains one definition code per parameter after the labels (0 not analysed, 1 free, 2 determined), always present and all 0 unless asked. The Rust decoder rejects unknown option bits and definition together with drag targets. The TypeScript decoder rejects a reply of the wrong length or with codes it cannot give. Those are codes outside 0 to 2, codes when not asked, a fixed parameter not determined, a parameter no equation reads not free, and analysed codes with an unavailable diagnosis. The sketch solver input gains an optional analyseDefinition, refused with a drag. A solved worker reply gains an optional diagnostics.definition of defined and under-defined point and entity IDs. It must be present exactly when asked, name only request points and entities, each once, and is refused on rejected replies. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. WebMCP tools keep their arguments. cad_inspect_sketch_constraints adds definition to point and entity rows and definition counts to its analysis summary, and its description and the public agent guide describe them. Its inspection solve asks for definition; edit, commit, preview and drag solves do not.
checklist.capabilities: No post, machine or sketch editing capability change. Constraint inspection reports which points and entities are fully defined.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. The bundled solver module grows from 225,165 to 253,394 bytes.
checklist.verification: tests/definition.rs checks that fixed parameters are determined and those no equation reads are free, that a full-rank group is all determined, and that a rectangle held only level and upright is free everywhere. It checks that a fixed corner and a width define the bottom corners alone, at the origin and 100,000 mm from it, with the width eliminated or solved whole and the corner fixed by value or by fixed parameters, and that a height then defines every corner. It checks that a circle needs its center and radius, that an arc with a fixed center and radius leaves its ends free, and that coordinates held only in sum are both free. A group whose constraint conflicts is not analysed, a drag cannot ask, and unknown options or versions are refused. A column that a free direction moves too little to tell is not analysed rather than called free, and one that a later free direction moves clearly is free. A sketch whose factor leaves out a coefficient of 5e-11, through which a free direction moves another point by about 5e-6, leaves that point not analysed rather than determined, alike in the rows and through the wire, while the columns it moves within the dependence distance are determined. Two equal lengths from nearly the same anchors, whose free direction moves a point by about 4.2e-10 per unit though rounding in the factor shows less, leave that point not analysed rather than determined, through the wire and through the solve's own rows in every column order. 20,000 seeded random groups with entries near the dependence distance check every analysed code against each column's distance from the rows' span. 20,000 seeded pairs of nearly parallel rows check every analysed code against the exact cross product of the rows, and every column they move by between the dependence distance and the certainty margin is not analysed. The probes take only their own allowance and analyse nothing without it, and each group is all determined exactly when its rank is full. Every sketch the Rust tests solve through the wire also checks that the codes are all 0 unless asked and that asking leaves every other reply word the same bit for bit. cadSketchNativeDefinition.test.ts checks with the native solver a rectangle whose driven bottom is defined and whose height is free, alike 100,000 mm from the origin and defined by a height, circles and arcs, expression coordinates and radii, the mapping of codes not analysed, that a point the factor's left-out coefficient lets move is unknown, never defined, beside one it moves within the dependence distance, which is defined, that the two equal lengths leave their moving point and its lines unknown, and that only inspection asks. cadSketchNativeSolver.test.ts, cadSketchNativeRuntime.test.ts and cadSketchSolverProtocol.test.ts check the options word, reply lengths, codes the solver cannot give, a drag refused before native code and the worker reply validation. cadSketchConstraintInspection.test.ts and useCadController.test.tsx check the row states, the summary counts, unknown rows after a rejected solve and the tool output. On the 26 benchmark workloads of up to 300 parameters, every analysed code agreed with a dense central-difference reference, and certifying each answer changes no code on any of the 30 workloads, so none loses a determined answer. Against the module 0.0.774 and 0.0.775 ship, in three runs of 15 rounds, every call was answered the same bit for bit, at ratios of 0.79 to 1.21 (median 1.00), with every group of at least 1 ms outside 0.95 to 1.05 faster, outliers both ways under 1 ms, and groups of at least 3 ms at 0.89 to 1.02. Against the 0.0.757 baseline the ratios are 0.37 to 1.07 (median 0.99). Asking costs about 2 µs for each full-rank group and 1.3 ms on the free die sketch. The full Vitest suite (551 files, 6209 tests), lint, ui:check, build, solver:check (187 Rust tests) and the release check pass, and e2e cad-sketch-constraints, cad-sketch-point-on-line, cad-sketch-symmetry, cad-sketch-tangent-joint, cad-sketch-linear-pattern and cad-workflow pass in Chromium.

publicNotes.summary: Agents can read which sketch geometry is fully defined.
changes: Constraint inspection for agents reports whether each sketch point and entity is fully defined, still free to move, or unknown, with counts for the whole sketch.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged. Sketch solving is unchanged. Agents that check inspection replies strictly must accept the new definition fields.
